# content-engine's copy lint, vendored

The deterministic copy lint on every public word: eyebrow and kicker labels,
asterisks, markdown emphasis, bracket tags, "generated by AI" notes and credit
lines, "Krish's take" labels, and his name. Krish, 28 October 2026: "don't add
stupid eyebrow text and asterisks and "generated by AI" and "Krish's take"
verbal diahorrea like you tend to. This needs to feel like a world class media
channel". And the same day: "Remember, no content refers to Krish, ever. I
still see that popping up from time to time. Even articles written are not
authored by Krish. My face only, for assets and the video format." Asked on
29 October whether another person called Krish may be named, he picked "Yes,
block it", so the name rule has no override.

content-engine owns the patterns. This engine only runs them, through
`engine/copy_lint.py`: `growth.py run lint` reports a hit in slot words as an
error, `growth.py social preflight` refuses a caption, or an asset's alt text,
that hits, `growth.py run release` holds any slot whose words, carried alt
text or titles hit, so nothing that hits it reaches Buffer, drafted pack
replies that hit are refused, and an audit repair whose new title, caption or
description hits is held; the Control Center loop holds a post draft that
hits rather than proposing it. Alt text is read as `carousel_text`, since it
carries the picture's words; titles as `titles`; everything else Growth writes
in public as `channel_copy`. Growth writes no article body, so it never reads
the `article_body` surface, but `engine/copy_lint.py` knows its name: an
unknown surface raises, and a raise holds every release.

## Where it came from

- Repository: `krishanraja/content-engine`
- Path: `config/copy-lint.json`
- Commit: `88847aa303741fad3886b38ace47a2e4d0c75f15` (branch
  `claude/fervent-brown-d8e55b`, 29 Oct 2026; if a squash merge gives it
  another commit on main, the sha256 below is the line that binds)
- Version: `2026-10-29.3`: adds the `no_name` pattern (his name, a spelling
  or handle of it, or a possessive of it, joined to a digit or an underscore
  too) and the `article_body` surface, which only `no_name` reads. Version
  `2026-10-29.2` added the pattern and the surface; `.3` widened the pattern.
  Before that, `2026-10-29.1` added "Krish's read" to `take_label` and the
  `illustration_label` pattern.
- sha256: `e04bb687c662b2bda0f47dbdde06b1358c3226e8d34b1e5862989987a64a3768`

The vendored file is byte for byte the upstream file. `tests/test_copy_lint.py`
checks its sha256 and version against the lines above, so a changed copy
cannot pass unnoticed.

## Updating it

1. Copy content-engine's `config/copy-lint.json` here unchanged.
2. Update the commit, version and sha256 above in the same commit.
3. Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests`. A pattern that now refuses an
   approved real post is content-engine's to fix there, never here.

## Known refusals to send upstream

True reporting about other people's AI work, MYMU's beat, that this version
refuses (found by Growth's review on 29 October 2026). They are
content-engine's to fix, in its copy-lint fixtures through
`docs/GROWTH-HANDOFF.md` there: exclude third-party subjects from the
provenance patterns, or list these as known refusals. Until then, a
rephrasing that keeps the meaning passes ("Sora generated every scene in
Coca-Cola's ad", "Veo 3 made this video").

| Sentence | Pattern |
|---|---|
| Coca-Cola's new ad: every scene was generated with AI | `ai_illustration_note` |
| This video was made with Veo 3. | `ai_self_note` |
| These images were generated by Midjourney for a fake Pope campaign. | `ai_self_note` |
| Her latest artwork was made in Canva. | `ai_illustration_note` |
| OpenAI's revenue (analysis: The Information) doubled. | `eyebrow_label` |
